gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, of ChatGPT's picks, only the $299 AT-LP70XBT ships with a stylus you can upgrade (any VM95 Series), while the JBL Spinner BT ($439.95 at Turntable Lab today) and the $259 AT-LP60XBT both play records on the same entry-level 3600L cartridge, so the JBL's 'replaceable cartridge' only helps after you buy a new cartridge.
standout_why: I read turntableverse.com (top result #1 and #2 in the two chats). Its table gives codecs, W&F <0.25% and S/N >55 dB for the AT-LP70XBT, and codecs for the Sony PS-LX3BT. It names no cartridge or stylus for any deck, names no weighting for the W&F figures and doesn't cover JBL. Neither cited rival was readable: WebFetch got only the page title from whathifi.com's Bluetooth turntable list and loudersound.com's best record players, and curl was not permitted. So I can't rule out that What Hi-Fi names the Spinner's AT3600L in its body text. I'm scoring this 2, not 3, for that reason.
decides: This confirms ChatGPT's choice of the AT-LP70XBT for most people. Of the three decks in its cards, it is the only one with a better cartridge (AT-VM95C) plus a stylus upgrade you can do without tools, and it costs $299. It also changes how the JBL Spinner BT should be pitched. At $439.95 it costs $140.95 more than the LP70XBT and $180.95 more than the LP60XBT. That extra pays for aptX HD, semi-automatic play, an adjustable counterweight and anti-skate, and a detachable headshell. It does not pay for a better cartridge: the stock AT3600L is the same family as the LP60XBT's ATN3600L stylus. Buyers who don't plan to fit another cartridge should pick the LP70XBT over the Spinner.
